name: AKUH,N Launches A Dedicated Breast Cancer Support Group

content.title: AKUH,N Launches A Dedicated Breast Cancer Support Group
content.summary: The group will meet monthly for peer support, workshops and learn coping strategies

content.text: The Aga Khan University Hospital, Nairobi (AKUH,N) has launched a dedicated Breast Cancer Support Group as a major step towards promoting the emotional and psychosocial support for breast cancer patients, survivors, and caregivers.
The support group will offer peer support, educational workshops, and coping strategies for people affected by breast cancer.

"We will be combating the big C (Cancer) with 3 Cs - Care, Compassion, Community and strive to instil hope in women who suffer from breast cancer," said Professor Mansoor Saleh, Chair of the Department of Haematology and Oncology. "The lessons and successes we observe in this breast cancer support group will inform the establishment of other cancer-specific support groups in the future."

According to Zahra Haji, the clinical psychologist who leads the psycho-oncology programme at AKUH,N, incorporating the support group into the cancer care will ensure that beyond addressing the physical challenges the hospital is also taking care of the emotional, spiritual, mental, financial, and social aspects of one's cancer journey.
"This ensures a true holistic approach to care, and is designed to be sustainable and responsive, continually evolving to meet the changing needs of our patients," she said.
Speaking at the launch ceremony, Mr Rashid Khalani, the Hospital's Chief Executive Officer emphasized the urgency of tackling the rising burden of cancer in Kenya.
"Non -communicable diseases (NCDs), especially cancer, have become very common among our populations. Today,

four out of ten deaths in Kenya are due to NCDs - something we are urgently working to address," he said. "This reality underscores the urgent need for collaboration and investment in advanced treatment technologies, research, and in training experts who can offer specialized care. Support groups like this one are a critical part of that ecosystem."
The group will meet monthly and is part of the hospital's broader mission to provide comprehensive, patient-centred cancer care.
